title: How to Use Study Halls and Free Periods in IB DP2
summary: Learn how to use study halls and free periods during the IB DP2 fall term to finish coursework, revise actively, and reduce work after school.
body_markdown:
To **use study halls and free periods** efficiently during the IB DP2 fall term, decide on one specific outcome before each period. Match short periods to retrieval, planning, or administrative tasks, and reserve longer blocks for exam questions or defined coursework milestones.


This matters especially from September to November, when tests, coursework, the Extended Essay, TOK, CAS, and university applications may overlap. The aim is consistent progress while preserving energy for lessons and after-school work.


### Why the IB DP2 fall term feels crowded


This period is difficult because you may be learning new content while revising DP1 topics, preparing for tests, and responding to coursework feedback.


The IB uses both **internal and external assessment** , but schools determine many internal calendars and interim deadlines. There is no universal September deadline for every IA, EE, or TOK component, so your coordinator's calendar is the source of truth. The[IB overview of Diploma Programme assessment](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/assessment-and-exams/) explains the distinction between examinations, internally assessed work, and externally assessed coursework.


Five productive 35-minute periods create almost three additional hours of focused work each week. Their value comes from consistency rather than one unusually long session.


### Build one system for choosing tasks


Do not begin by opening several platforms and deciding what feels urgent. Maintain one master list of deadlines, coursework milestones, tests, applications, and personal commitments.


A practical priority order is:


1. **Urgent assessed work** , such as a submission due within several days.
2. **Blocked work** , where one action will allow later progress, such as asking about unclear feedback.
3. **High-value revision** , especially weak topics appearing in an approaching assessment.
4. **Maintenance tasks** , including flashcards, citations, file organization, and CAS records.


Use the[RevisionDojo IB Study Planner](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/study-planner) or another calendar to assign tasks to periods. Schedule an outcome, such as “complete two integration questions and mark them,” rather than “study maths.”
